brand.name: Industry Next Communications Lab
brand.description: An independent research program exploring practical communication between people, places and intelligent systems.
brand.status: Proposed 2026/2027 program. Project explorations, not live employment offers.
brand.affiliation: Independent of Nokia Bell Labs, AT&T and their affiliates. No affiliation or endorsement is implied.

typography.labels: IBM Plex Mono if separately supplied; otherwise ui-monospace / monospace

principles: Publish only what can be explained and shared safely
brand.projectStatusNote: Pay, hours, eligibility, supervisor, location, agreements and legal review must be resolved before recruitment or work begins. Budgets are illustrative materials estimates in USD, exclude labor, tax and shipping, and are not spending authorization.
brand.pointcastNote: PointCast is an exploratory program context; exact place, partner and installation permissions remain to be confirmed.

projects.title: Local messages that survive a disconnect
projects.question: Can two local devices reconcile messages without losing a confirmed note?
projects.oneWeek: Build a two-client prototype with synthetic messages. Disconnect one client, create conflicting edits, reconnect and log 20 trials.
projects.fourWeek: Add explicit conflict choices, export and a reproducible three-device test.
projects.safety: Use invented messages. Keep the demo on a trusted local network; no identity claims or production encryption claims.
projects.deliverable: Runnable demo, event log, conflict policy and two-page findings
projects.successMeasure: Zero lost confirmed messages in the 20 scripted trials; all conflicts visible
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor reviews storage and threat model. Mike approves any external pilot; agents propose tests and never read personal messages.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: Community radio listening desk
projects.question: How can a listening guide make a lawful public broadcast easier to discover?
projects.oneWeek: Compare three layouts using licensed sample audio or lawful public streams; record completion time for 10 scripted lookup tasks.
projects.fourWeek: Build an accessible schedule browser with provenance and a small editorial workflow.
projects.safety: No RF transmission, private-signal interception or rebroadcast. Check stream permissions before embedding or recording.
projects.deliverable: Receive-only listening prototype and source-permissions ledger
projects.successMeasure: At least 9 of 10 lookup tasks completed; every audio source has a documented permission basis
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor approves sources and equipment. Human review is required before public audio or any recording of people.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: A quiet ambient status display
projects.question: Can a glanceable display convey useful status without becoming surveillance?
projects.oneWeek: Prototype three paper or browser states for shared equipment availability using synthetic events; test label comprehension internally.
projects.fourWeek: Add an optional low-voltage e-paper display and user-controlled quiet hours.
projects.safety: No cameras, microphones, people tracking or mains wiring. Use status and text as well as color.
projects.deliverable: State vocabulary, browser prototype and installation sketch
projects.successMeasure: Four of five consenting adult testers identify each state within five seconds
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor approves any hardware and placement. Mike approves public installation; agents cannot infer people’s presence.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: Accessible message repair
projects.question: Which error message best helps a person recover from a failed send?
projects.oneWeek: Create keyboard-first send/error/retry flows with screen-reader labels. Run 12 scripted keyboard and announcement checks.
projects.fourWeek: Co-design revisions with consenting adult participants under an approved accessibility test plan.
projects.skills: HTML, CSS, accessibility testing, plain language
projects.safety: Do not infer disability or collect medical data. Participation is optional; record only necessary anonymous observations.
projects.deliverable: Accessible prototype and keyboard/screen-reader test sheet
projects.successMeasure: All 12 checks pass; failures remain understandable without color or sound
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor signs off test design and consent. Human approval precedes participant recruitment and recording.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: An agent handoff you can inspect
projects.question: What must a handoff contain so another agent can continue without inventing authority?
projects.oneWeek: Define a handoff schema: task, evidence, permissions, unknowns and stop condition. Compare it against free text on 20 synthetic tasks.
projects.fourWeek: Add validation, replay traces and a human approval checkpoint for external actions.
projects.safety: Use synthetic tasks and redact secrets. No autonomous sending, purchases or permission escalation.
projects.deliverable: Schema, validation tests and scored evaluation set
projects.successMeasure: Every blocked action stays blocked; at least 18 of 20 handoffs preserve the stated next step
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor reviews rubric and API cap. Humans approve consequential actions; agents can draft and test within the sandbox.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: Offline field notes that come home
projects.question: How can notes remain usable offline and merge predictably later?
projects.oneWeek: Build a local notebook with timestamps and export. Run 15 airplane-mode/edit/reconnect scenarios using invented field observations.
projects.fourWeek: Add conflict comparison and a portable archive with attachment checksums.
projects.skills: Web storage, file formats, UX testing
projects.safety: No real location trails, private field observations or participant identifiers. Test deletion and explain local-device exposure.
projects.deliverable: Offline demo, export specimen and recovery instructions
projects.successMeasure: All 15 scenarios preserve original text; a second machine opens the export
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor reviews data lifecycle and merge rules. Any real field study requires human approval and a data plan.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: Public data with visible uncertainty
projects.question: Can a small dashboard explain stale or missing public sensor readings honestly?
projects.oneWeek: Choose one appropriately licensed public dataset; cache a snapshot and prototype current, stale, missing and suspect states.
projects.fourWeek: Compare two aggregation methods and publish reproducible transformations with attribution.
projects.skills: Data cleaning, chart design, basic statistics
projects.safety: Use public non-personal data only. No location inference about people and no emergency, health or safety guidance.
projects.deliverable: Dashboard prototype, license record and transformation notebook
projects.successMeasure: Every chart shows unit, source and timestamp; all four failure states are visibly distinct
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor approves dataset and uncertainty language. Mike approves publication; agents may summarize but cannot certify accuracy.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: Translation with a visible review step
projects.question: Where do short community notices lose meaning during translation?
projects.oneWeek: Write 20 invented notices; compare draft translations with qualified human review for names, dates, instructions and ambiguity.
projects.fourWeek: Add a glossary, side-by-side editor and disagreement log for two reviewed languages.
projects.materialsBudget: $0–40 materials; human review must be separately budgeted
projects.safety: No sensitive notices, medical/legal advice or real personal data. Do not label machine output as human-verified.
projects.deliverable: Reviewable prototype, glossary and error taxonomy
projects.successMeasure: All names, dates and instructions match after human review; uncertainty remains visible
projects.approvalBoundary: A qualified human reviewer is required for each language. Mike approves any public translation; agents only draft.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: A small archive you can reopen
projects.question: What is the simplest durable record of a research experiment?
projects.oneWeek: Package one synthetic experiment as README, open-format data, assets and checksums. Ask a second person to follow it on a clean folder.
projects.fourWeek: Add versioned manifests, consent/license fields and a migration checklist.
projects.safety: No proprietary work, participant identities or unlicensed media. State retention and deletion limits before real archiving.
projects.deliverable: Portable archive, manifest schema and recovery report
projects.successMeasure: A second person locates evidence and reproduces the sample result without author help
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor approves licensing and retention. Human approval is required before archiving real personal or third-party records.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: Useful interfaces on a thin connection
projects.question: Which content is truly necessary when a connection is slow or unreliable?
projects.oneWeek: Create a text-first notice page; simulate 400 kbps and 400 ms latency with cache disabled. Compare against a heavier baseline.
projects.fourWeek: Add offline fallback, resilient form-free navigation and a documented asset budget.
projects.safety: Use synthetic content and local network simulation. No covert analytics or live user profiling.
projects.deliverable: Working prototype, trace captures and byte-budget report
projects.successMeasure: Core text usable within five seconds in 9 of 10 controlled runs; no broken keyboard navigation
projects.approvalBoundary: Mentor validates measurement setup. Mike approves deployment and any analytics; agents may run synthetic checks only.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: PointCast community bulletin
projects.question: Can a shared bulletin make a small place easier to navigate without gathering personal data?
projects.oneWeek: Mock a PointCast-area bulletin with five invented notices, expiry dates and clear source labels. Run 10 find-and-verify tasks.
projects.fourWeek: Build moderation, expiry and correction views; explore a print companion and local cache.
projects.safety: PointCast is a program context, not a verified venue partnership. No real names, addresses, contact forms or live submissions.
projects.deliverable: Bulletin prototype, moderation checklist and print sheet
projects.successMeasure: At least 9 of 10 tasks find the right notice; every notice shows source and expiry
projects.approvalBoundary: Mike confirms the place, partners and permissions before any installation. Human moderation approves every real public notice.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

projects.title: The reproducibility relay
projects.question: Can a new teammate repeat a result from the record alone?
projects.oneWeek: Take another project’s synthetic dataset and instructions. Re-run three key tests independently and document discrepancies.
projects.fourWeek: Build a reusable evidence checklist, comparison report and release gate across four projects.
projects.safety: Only use approved synthetic/public data. Do not copy secrets into logs or let agents mark their own work independently verified.
projects.deliverable: Independent replication note, annotated checklist and corrected instructions
projects.successMeasure: Three tests reproduce within declared tolerance or yield an explicit, actionable failure report
projects.approvalBoundary: A human mentor defines tolerances and reviews discrepancies. Mike decides release; agents help execute but do not approve themselves.
projects.status: Project exploration • not an employment offer

roles.Mike: Proposed sponsor and scope owner; confirms supervisor, budget, partnerships and release authority before launch.
roles.Interns: Proposed supervised researchers; scope, pay and working terms must be settled before any work begins.
roles.Agents: Assist with research, synthetic data, code, tests and documentation; cannot replace human supervision, consent or approval.

cadence: Before launch: confirm pay, hours, supervisor, eligibility, location and legal terms.
2026 proposal: choose one or two low-risk pilots, finalize scope and prepare safe fixtures.
One-week experiment: question, baseline, small build, repeated test, evidence review.
Four-week stretch: refine, independently reproduce, document and seek release approval.
2027 proposal: revisit successful pilots with mentors; publish only verified results and limitations.
